summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the investable universe around HVDC transformer winding inputs and qualification-dependent grid-OEM supply chains. For US-listed exposure, the cleanest reference anchors are large-cap HVDC transformer OEMs or grid-equipment leaders, while the underfollowed lane is weaker but potentially interesting: transformer makers, transmission hardware suppliers, and transformer testing/diagnostic vendors that benefit from grid buildout, long qualification cycles, and utility/OEM procurement friction. No US-listed pure-play CTC or paper-insulated copper conductor supplier was confirmed in the provided evidence; pure-play evidence currently appears stronger in India via KSH International, which is not US-listed. Layer 1B expansion found very limited clean US-listed exposure to continuously transposed conductor or paper-insulated transformer winding inputs. The most direct public-market anchors are large OEM/grid-equipment names that consume or integrate these inputs, while the underfollowed lane is more likely to sit in adjacent qualified utility hardware and component suppliers rather than pure CTC. KSH International remains the clearest seed for the India HVDC/CTC chokepoint, but it is not US-listed. For US-listed research, PLPC is the most plausible underfollowed second-order candidate because utility-specified transmission hardware can share the same approval/specification-lock characteristics, although it is not a transformer-winding supplier.
